test_cases.title: Nav App Executes at 100 Hz on Static Schedule
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app with mocked TDM scheduler, mocked software bus, and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test. Configure scheduler to drive nav app at 100 Hz over a one-second simulated interval.
procedure: Run the scheduler for 1.000 seconds of simulated time.
Count the number of times the nav app Execute() entry point is invoked.
Record the timestamps of each invocation.
Compute the mean inter-invocation period.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Nav app Execute() is invoked exactly 100 times in 1.000 simulated seconds, and the mean period equals 10.000 ms within 1 microsecond tolerance.

test_cases.title: Nav App Subscribes to IMU Messages
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app with mocked software bus that records all subscribe calls, and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test.
procedure: Invoke the nav app initialization entry point.
Inspect the recorded list of subscriptions on the mocked bus.
Verify a subscription exists with the IMU message topic identifier.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The mocked software bus records exactly one subscription whose topic identifier matches the IMU message type after nav app initialization.

test_cases.title: Nav App Subscribes to Barometer Messages
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app with mocked software bus that records all subscribe calls, and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test.
procedure: Invoke the nav app initialization entry point.
Inspect the recorded list of subscriptions on the mocked bus.
Verify a subscription exists with the barometric altimeter message topic identifier.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The mocked software bus records exactly one subscription whose topic identifier matches the barometer message type after nav app initialization.

test_cases.title: Nav App Subscribes to GPS Fix Messages
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app with mocked software bus that records all subscribe calls, and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test.
procedure: Invoke the nav app initialization entry point.
Inspect the recorded list of subscriptions on the mocked bus.
Verify a subscription exists with the GPS fix message topic identifier.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The mocked software bus records exactly one subscription whose topic identifier matches the GPS fix message type after nav app initialization.

test_cases.title: Nav State Published at 100 Hz on Software Bus
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app with mocked software bus and scheduler driving nav app at 100 Hz, and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test. Mocked bus records all publish calls. Provide nominal IMU/baro/GPS inputs throughout.
procedure: Run the scheduler for 1.000 seconds of simulated time.
Filter recorded publish calls to those whose topic equals the navigation state message topic.
Count the filtered publishes and compute their mean inter-publish period.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Exactly 100 navigation state messages are published during 1.000 simulated seconds, and the mean inter-publish period equals 10.000 ms within 1 microsecond tolerance.

test_cases.title: Published Nav State Contains Sixteen-State Composition
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app with mocked software bus and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test. Provide one cycle of nominal IMU/baro/GPS inputs.
procedure: Run a single nav app Execute() cycle.
Capture the navigation state message published on the mocked bus.
Inspect the message payload structure and field names.
Verify the payload contains position, velocity, attitude quaternion, accelerometer bias, and gyroscope bias fields.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The published navigation state message payload contains all of: 3-element position, 3-element velocity, 4-element attitude quaternion, 3-element accelerometer bias, and 3-element gyroscope bias.

test_cases.title: Nav State Carries Monotonic Microsecond Timestamp
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app with mocked software bus, a fake time source providing monotonic microsecond ticks, and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test. Schedule nav app for 100 cycles at 100 Hz.
procedure: Run 100 nav app Execute() cycles.
Collect the timestamp field from each published navigation state message.
Verify each timestamp is strictly greater than the previous timestamp.
Verify timestamp units match microseconds by comparing successive deltas to the configured 10000 us period.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All 100 timestamps are strictly monotonically increasing, and successive deltas equal 10000 microseconds within 1 microsecond tolerance.

test_cases.title: Validity Flag Published With Each Nav State Message
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app with mocked software bus and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test. Provide nominal sensor inputs and run multiple cycles.
procedure: Run 10 nav app Execute() cycles.
Inspect the publish records on the mocked software bus.
Verify that for each navigation state message there is a corresponding validity flag publication (or validity field) with the same timestamp.
Verify the validity flag is observable as a boolean-valued field on the bus.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every navigation state message published on the bus is accompanied by a validity flag value with the same timestamp.

test_cases.title: Validity Flag False When Required Inputs Are Missing
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app with mocked software bus, configurable sensor input injectors for IMU, baro, and GPS, and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test.
procedure: Run 50 cycles with all required sensor inputs present and record validity flag values.
Stop injecting IMU messages and run 50 additional cycles, recording validity flag values.
Resume injecting IMU messages and run 50 more cycles, recording validity flag values.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Validity flag is true during all cycles in phase 1, transitions to false within one cycle of inputs becoming unavailable in phase 2, and returns to true in phase 3 after inputs are restored.

test_cases.title: Nav State Continues Publishing at 100 Hz With Missing Inputs
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app with mocked software bus, configurable sensor input injectors, and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test. Drive scheduler at 100 Hz.
procedure: Run 100 cycles with all sensor inputs nominal.
Disable GPS injection and run 100 cycles.
Disable both GPS and barometer injection and run 100 cycles.
Disable all sensor injection and run 100 cycles.
Count navigation state publishes per phase and compute the mean period.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each phase produces exactly 100 navigation state publishes with mean period 10.000 ms within 1 microsecond tolerance, regardless of which sensor inputs are unavailable.

test_cases.title: Published Position Stays Within Configured Bound of GPS Fix
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app with mocked software bus, a recorded sensor input dataset (IMU, baro, GPS) representative of an FT1 flight profile, and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test. Configure the divergence bound parameter to its mission value.
procedure: Replay the recorded sensor dataset through the nav app for the full duration.
For each published navigation state, compute the horizontal distance between the published position and the most recent GPS fix on the bus.
Record the maximum horizontal distance observed across the run.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The maximum horizontal distance between published position and the latest GPS fix never exceeds the configured divergence bound for the entire dataset.

test_cases.title: Position Divergence Bound Hardware Demonstration
test_cases.setup: Pico2 flight board powered with GPS, IMU, and barometer connected. Telemetry logger capturing software bus traffic. Outdoor location with clear sky view. Divergence bound configured to mission value.
procedure: Power the flight board and confirm boot log on the serial console.
Wait for GPS fix acquisition and confirm validity flag transitions to true on the telemetry log.
Walk the board on a 100 meter horizontal path at walking pace for at least 5 minutes while logging all bus traffic.
Stop the run and save the telemetry log to file.
Run the post-processing script to compute, for each nav state, the horizontal distance to the latest GPS fix.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Across the entire logged run, the maximum horizontal distance between published navigation position and the latest GPS fix never exceeds the configured divergence bound; the post-processing plot shows the bound is respected throughout.

expected_artifacts.name: divergence_plot.png

test_cases.title: POSIX and Pico2 Builds Produce Identical Nav State Outputs
test_cases.setup: Build nav app for both POSIX and Pico2 targets from the same source tree, with a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test. Prepare a deterministic recorded sensor input dataset (IMU, baro, GPS).
procedure: Replay the dataset through the POSIX build and capture every published navigation state message to file A.
Replay the same dataset through the Pico2 build (or its host-emulated equivalent) and capture every published navigation state message to file B.
Diff file A and file B byte-for-byte on the published nav state payload fields and timestamps.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: File A and file B contain the same number of records and every nav state field (position, velocity, attitude quaternion, biases, timestamp, validity) matches byte-for-byte across both builds.

test_cases.title: Deterministic Nav Output Across Repeated Runs
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app on POSIX build with mocked software bus and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test. Prepare a fixed recorded sensor input dataset.
procedure: Replay the dataset through a fresh nav app instance and capture every published nav state message to file R1.
Tear down and re-initialize the nav app, replay the same dataset, and capture nav state messages to file R2.
Repeat once more to produce file R3.
Diff R1, R2, and R3 byte-for-byte on the nav state payload fields and timestamps.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: R1, R2, and R3 are byte-for-byte identical across all nav state payload fields and timestamps.

test_cases.title: Validity Flag True Under Nominal Inputs
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app with mocked software bus, steady nominal IMU, baro, and GPS injection, and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test.
procedure: Run 200 nav app Execute() cycles.
Collect every validity flag value published with each navigation state.
Verify all 200 validity flag values are true.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All 200 published validity flag values are true while all required inputs are present.

test_cases.title: Nav State Schedule Holds Across Long Run
test_cases.setup: Initialize nav app with mocked software bus, scheduler driving nav app at 100 Hz, and a stubbed nav_lib whose outputs are controllable from the test. Provide nominal sensor inputs throughout.
procedure: Run the scheduler for 60.000 seconds of simulated time.
Count Execute() invocations and navigation state publish events.
Compute the maximum jitter (max deviation from 10.000 ms) of the inter-publish interval.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Exactly 6000 Execute() invocations and 6000 navigation state publishes occur, and maximum inter-publish jitter is below 10 microseconds.

test_cases.title: Boost-Phase Update Skipping Verification
test_cases.setup: Construct nav_app with: stub broker (delivers IMU/baro/GPS samples + a JUNO_MSG_AFM_PHASE_T with ePhase=JUNO_PHASE_BOOST), stub nav_lib (test vtable that records every UpdateBaro/UpdateGps/PredictImu call), stub time. Initialize nav_app via NavAppInit; OnStart returns SUCCESS.
procedure: Inject a JUNO_MSG_AFM_PHASE_T with ePhase=JUNO_PHASE_BOOST into the broker.
Call nav_app's OnProcess hook three times (3 x 10 ms ticks).
On each tick the broker delivers one IMU sample, one baro sample, and one GPS fix.
Inspect the stub nav_lib call log.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: stub nav_lib received 3 PredictImu calls (one per tick, IMU updates always allowed). stub nav_lib received ZERO UpdateBaro calls and ZERO UpdateGps calls during BOOST. nav_app returns JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS on every OnProcess invocation. JUNO_MSG_NAV_STATE_T published on every tick with bValid forwarded from stub nav_lib.

test_cases.title: Post-Boost Settling Window for Sensor Re-Enablement
test_cases.setup: Construct nav_app with: stub broker (delivers a phase-transition sequence BOOST -> APOGEE), stub nav_lib (records every UpdateBaro/UpdateGps call), stub time (allows time-warping for the test). NavAppInit + OnStart succeed.
procedure: Inject JUNO_MSG_AFM_PHASE_T with ePhase=JUNO_PHASE_BOOST; advance 5 ticks while delivering IMU/baro/GPS samples (no Update calls expected).
Inject JUNO_MSG_AFM_PHASE_T with ePhase=JUNO_PHASE_APOGEE; record the boost-exit time as t_exit.
Advance time by 0.5 seconds (50 x 10 ms ticks); on each tick deliver IMU/baro/GPS samples and call OnProcess. Verify NO UpdateBaro/UpdateGps calls (still inside settling window).
Advance time to (t_exit + 1.001 seconds); call OnProcess; deliver IMU/baro/GPS.
Continue for 3 more ticks; verify UpdateBaro and UpdateGps are now called on every tick.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: During the 0.5-second post-boost interval, stub nav_lib received ZERO UpdateBaro and ZERO UpdateGps calls. After (t_exit + 1.0 s), stub nav_lib received UpdateBaro and UpdateGps calls on every subsequent tick. PredictImu called on every OnProcess invocation throughout. nav_app returned JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS throughout.
